recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-5599 unless a future terminology decision changes the FilterOperator code set.
issue_request: FHIR-5599 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 ValueSet issue requesting that the inconsistent FilterOperator code "not in" be renamed to "not-in", with a 2015-03-09 MnM/FHIR block vote recorded in the Jira resolution.
initial_application: No commit on the current git history is tagged with FHIR-5599. The Jira comment says the work was already done for another task, and commit e995abe5d075934abc6de37f9449f057bcfbb82e (#5573: remove spaces from internally defined codes) changed the ValueSet spreadsheet filter-operator entries from "not in" to "not-in" before FHIR-5599 was resolved.
additional_context: ValueSet is an active resource in source/fhir.ini. The current ValueSet StructureDefinition required-binds ValueSet.compose.include.filter.op to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/filter-operator and lists not-in in the operator summary. The current FilterOperator CodeSystem defines code value not-in, and ValueSet notes document op values in and not-in. Focused source searches found no stale operator-code spelling of not in. Community searches found no exact FHIR-5599 discussion affecting this conclusion; apparent FHIR-5599 hits were later unrelated issue keys such as FHIR-55991 and FHIR-55992.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch because the authoritative current source already reflects the requested spelling and no source edit remains.

related_jiras.note: The #5573 implementation commit removed spaces from internally defined codes and appears to be the other task that applied FHIR-5599, but FHIR-5573 is broader and was not independently reconciled here.
